composition.value: A 2×2 grid of four 640×360 cells (each exactly 50% × 50% of the frame) with no gutter, border or shared background: the cell edges are made only by the colour change between grounds. Each cell is composed as its own centred 16:9 film. The hero object (face, pill, prompt card, promise line) sits on the cell's vertical centre line, 45–55% across, so the four focal points form a rectangle about 320 px in from each frame edge, and the eye's jump between cells is always the same length. At the start the top row is light (#F8F8F8, #EAECF0) and the bottom row saturated or dark (sky, navy). From 5.0 to 7.6 s all four cells are light. After 7.633 s the dark cell is top right, and from 9.65 s bottom right too. A dark cell is always diagonal to or below the lightest one, and in 9.65–11.6 the darks sit in the right column.

materials.value: Each cell has its own material. TL: a matte off-white ground with a glossy, soft-shaded 3D-looking sphere character (cyan-to-mint radial gradient, specular top left) and a white pill search field. TR: a paper-flat ground with a cut-out photo collage and flat pastel rectangles (no shadows), then a smoke plate. BL: a frosted glass card (white at about 40% opacity with a white rim) over a photographic sky with clouds, then light interface screens and a warm gradient placeholder. BR: a dark glass pill with a cyan rim light on a navy-to-teal gradient, a glossy blue round button, then a white chat with blurred-glow avatars and, at the end, translucent white email cards on navy.

lighting.value: Mostly flat interface light with no cast shadows. There are three lit moments. BR: a soft blue light streak sweeps under the display word (F9–F78), and a cyan rim light rides the pill. TR: an overexposed white light leak washes the photo collage out to white (F267–F311). BR: a click is marked by a white ring ripple round the button (F267–F275).

styleSummary: A quad-split portfolio clip: four clean AI-product promos (light interface style, glass, gradients, one 3D-shaded mascot) play side by side with no frame between them. Each runs abstract opening, then character or problem, then real interface. Their cuts are staggered and paired on diagonals, so the grid never changes all at once. Most animation is drawn on twos (30 drawings a second inside a 60 fps file); every line is typed or built on screen.
